key: Fight in the way of Allah against those who fight against you, but begin not hostilities. Lo! Allah loveth not aggressors.
s: The verse opens the ayahs that command the believers to fight, slay and drive out those who fight them; al-Tabari, on 2:190, takes the command as unrepealed and reads the forbidden aggression as killing women, children or those who pay tribute.

evidence.words: وأولى هذين القولين بالصواب، القولُ الذي قاله عمر بن عبد العزيز. لأن دعوى المدَّعي نَسْخَ آية يحتمل أن تكون غيرَ منسوخة، بغير دلالة على صحة دعواه، تحكُّم … فمعنى قوله:"ولا تعتدوا": لا تقتلوا وليدًا ولا امرأةً، ولا من أعطاكم الجزية من أهل الكتابَين والمجوس
evidence.gloss: The sounder of these two views is the one ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz held (that the verse is not repealed, and that the transgression forbidden is against women, children and those who have not made war), since to claim that a verse which may well be unrepealed has been repealed, with no proof of the claim, is arbitrary … So the meaning of ‘and do not transgress’ is: do not kill a child or a woman, nor any who have given you the jizya (tribute) of the people of the two Books and the Magians.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Baqarah 2:190, at 196). Plain sense faithful to day.js: 2:190 to 2:193 command fighting those who fight, slaying them where found and driving them out; stated in one plain clause, no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 2:190 al-Tabari gives two views (the ayah was the first on fighting and was repealed by Bara’a; or it stands unrepealed and the forbidden transgression is the killing of women and children), then prefers the view of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz because claiming repeal without proof is arbitrary, and glosses wa-la taʿtadu as: do not kill a child, a woman, or anyone who has given the jizya among the people of the two Books and the Magians. The sentence carries both points, and the limit he sets, without drift; it does not import Pickthall’s ‘begin not hostilities’. Evidence pieces re-found by squashed string match in the packet. 41 words; entry-check ok.
